theory.intro: Rounding replaces a number with the nearest 'round' number — a multiple of $10$, $100$, $1000$ and so on.
facts: Look at the digit **just to the right** of the rounding place.
If it is $5$ or more, round **up**; if it is $4$ or less, round **down**.
Every digit after the rounding place becomes $0$.
steps: Underline the digit in the place you are rounding to.
Check the next digit on its right.
Round up or stay, then fill the rest with zeros.

workedExamples.question_text:
Round:
(a) $38\,274\,613$ to the nearest hundred
(b) $6\,853\,274$ to the nearest hundred thousand.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $38\,274\,\underline{6}13$. The tens digit is $1$, so keep the hundreds digit and replace the tens and ones with zeros.
$38\,274\,613\approx38\,274\,600$
(b) $6\,\underline{8}53\,274$. The ten-thousands digit is $5$, so round the hundred-thousands digit up.
$6\,853\,274\approx6\,900\,000$

$47\,99\underline{9}\,684$
The hundreds digit is $6$, so round up. The next thousand after $47\,999\,000$ is $48\,000\,000$.
$47\,999\,684\approx48\,000\,000$

workedExamples.question_text: $286\,743\,519$ was rounded to $286\,740\,000$. To which place was it rounded?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Rounding to the nearest ten thousand keeps the ten-thousands digit $4$, because the next digit is $3$.
$286\,7\underline{4}3\,519\approx286\,740\,000$
It was rounded to the nearest ten thousand.

workedExamples.question_text:
A whole-number count rounds to $12\,700\,000$ to the nearest hundred thousand. Find:
(a) the smallest possible count
(b) the largest possible count.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Halfway between $12\,600\,000$ and $12\,700\,000$ is $12\,650\,000$. It rounds up to $12\,700\,000$, so this is the smallest.
(b) $12\,750\,000$ is the next halfway value and rounds up to $12\,800\,000$. The largest whole number before it is $12\,749\,999$.

workedExamples.question_text: A count rounds to $59\,380\,000$ to the nearest ten thousand and to $59\,400\,000$ to the nearest hundred thousand. Give one possible original count and check it.
workedExamples.solution_text:
One possible count is $59\,382\,617$.
To the nearest ten thousand, the next digit is $2$, so
$59\,382\,617\approx59\,380\,000$.
To the nearest hundred thousand, the next digit is $8$, so
$59\,382\,617\approx59\,400\,000$.
It satisfies both rounding statements.

Round $3\,764\,210$ to the nearest ten thousand.

A region's population is $6\,581\,900$.
Round it to the nearest hundred thousand.

development.question_text:
A national census records $24\,650\,000$ people.
Round this to the nearest million.
Round the surveyed distance $7\,999\,650$ m to the nearest thousand metres.
Round $82\,149\,999$ to the nearest ten thousand.
A map gives a route length of $1\,250\,000$ m. Round it to the nearest hundred thousand metres.
Which place was $73\,846\,219$ rounded to if the result is $73\,800\,000$?
development.solution_text:
The last five digits became zero, so the hundred-thousands digit was rounded.
The number was rounded to the nearest hundred thousand.

development.question_text:
A population of $54\,499\,999$ is reported to the nearest million.
What is the rounded population?

mastery.question_text:
A whole-number census count rounds to $8\,300\,000$ to the nearest hundred thousand.
What is the smallest possible count?
mastery.solution_text:
The halfway point below $8\,300\,000$ is $8\,250\,000$.
Smallest possible count $=8\,250\,000$

mastery.question_text:
A whole-number distance rounds to $47\,000$ m to the nearest thousand metres.
What is the largest possible distance?
mastery.solution_text:
$47\,500$ m would round up to $48\,000$ m.
Largest possible distance $=47\,499$ m

mastery.question_text:
A report rounds the same count to $6\,420\,000$ to the nearest ten thousand and to $6\,400\,000$ to the nearest hundred thousand.
Give one possible original count.
mastery.solution_text:
$6\,421\,000$ rounds to $6\,420\,000$ to the nearest ten thousand.
It also rounds to $6\,400\,000$ to the nearest hundred thousand.
One possible count is $6\,421\,000$.
